FD_DATASYNC: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_datasync. If PATH_OPEN is set, includes the right to invoke path_open with fdflags_t.dsync.

FD_READ: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_read and sock_recv. If FD_SEEK is set, includes the right to invoke fd_pread.

FD_SEEK: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_seek. This flag implies FD_TELL.

FD_FDSTAT_SET_FLAGS: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_fdstat_set_flags.

FD_SYNC: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_sync. If PATH_OPEN is set, includes the right to invoke path_open with fdflags_t.RSYNC and fdflags_t.DSYNC.

FD_TELL: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_seek in such a way that the file offset remains unaltered (i.e. whence_t.CUR with offset zero), or to invoke fd_tell.

FD_WRITE: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_write and sock_send. If FD_SEEK is set, includes the right to invoke fd_pwrite.

FD_ADVISE: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_advise.

FD_ALLOCATE: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_allocate.

PATH_CREATE_DIRECTORY: bool = false

The right to invoke path_create_directory.

PATH_CREATE_FILE: bool = false

If PATH_OPEN is set, the right to invoke path_open with oflags_t.CREAT.

PATH_LINK_SOURCE: bool = false

The right to invoke path_link with the file descriptor as the source directory.

PATH_LINK_TARGET: bool = false

The right to invoke path_link with the file descriptor as the target directory.

PATH_OPEN: bool = false

The right to invoke path_open.

FD_READDIR: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_readdir.

PATH_READLINK: bool = false

The right to invoke path_readlink.

PATH_RENAME_SOURCE: bool = false

The right to invoke path_rename with the file descriptor as the source directory.

PATH_RENAME_TARGET: bool = false

The right to invoke path_rename with the file descriptor as the target directory.

PATH_FILESTAT_GET: bool = false

The right to invoke path_filestat_get.

PATH_FILESTAT_SET_SIZE: bool = false

The right to change a file's size. If PATH_OPEN is set, includes the right to invoke path_open with oflags_t.TRUNC. Note: there is no function named path_filestat_set_size. This follows POSIX design, which only has ftruncate and does not provide ftruncateat. While such function would be desirable from the API design perspective, there are virtually no use cases for it since no code written for POSIX systems would use it. Moreover, implementing it would require multiple syscalls, leading to inferior performance.

PATH_FILESTAT_SET_TIMES: bool = false

The right to invoke path_filestat_set_times.

FD_FILESTAT_GET: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_filestat_get.

FD_FILESTAT_SET_SIZE: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_filestat_set_size.

FD_FILESTAT_SET_TIMES: bool = false

The right to invoke fd_filestat_set_times.

PATH_SYMLINK: bool = false

The right to invoke path_symlink.

PATH_REMOVE_DIRECTORY: bool = false

The right to invoke path_remove_directory.

PATH_UNLINK_FILE: bool = false

The right to invoke path_unlink_file.

POLL_FD_READWRITE: bool = false

//! wasi_snapshot_preview1 spec available (in witx format) here:
//! * typenames -- https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI/blob/main/legacy/preview1/witx/typenames.witx
//! * module -- https://github.com/WebAssembly/WASI/blob/main/legacy/preview1/witx/wasi_snapshot_preview1.witx
//! Note that libc API does *not* go in this file. wasi libc API goes into std/c.zig instead.
const builtin = @import("builtin");
const std = @import("std");
const assert = std.debug.assert;

comptime {
    if (builtin.os.tag == .wasi) {
        assert(@alignOf(i8) == 1);
        assert(@alignOf(u8) == 1);
        assert(@alignOf(i16) == 2);
        assert(@alignOf(u16) == 2);
        assert(@alignOf(i32) == 4);
        assert(@alignOf(u32) == 4);
        assert(@alignOf(i64) == 8);
        assert(@alignOf(u64) == 8);
    }
}
